claims.value: SILAC light / SILAC medium / SILAC heavy
claims.evidence: mqpar.xml multiplicity=3, labelMods: '' (light), 'Arg6;Lys4' (medium), 'Arg10;Lys8' (heavy). proteinGroups.txt has Intensity L/M/H for every experiment; in lanes A, B, C all three channels carry comparable signal (e.g. Expt1_B L 4.1e11, M 3.3e11, H 3.0e11) lane C therefore gets three rows per file; in lanes D the M channel is ~4% of L/H (Expt1_D M 2.9e10 vs L 7.6e11, H 6.4e11) and Supp Data 1 uses only L/H for Expt1_D, so D is annotated as a 2-channel (L/H) run. Terms PRIDE:0000326/0000327/0000325 verified in OLS.

Description of Supplementary Files (Supp Data 1 legend): 'Cells were warmed to 37 C in the presence (light labelled cells; L) or absence (heavy labelled cells; H) of HGF'. Supp Data 1 header 'Ratio L/H Normalized Expt1_C C/B (Nuc HGF/Nuc Ctl)' and 'Ratio L/M ... C/A (Int Nucl HGF/No int nuclear)' (same for Expt2_C): the L channel of lane C is the internalised +HGF nuclear sample. Methods: 'Light-labelled cells were warmed to 37 C for 30 min ... in the presence of HGF (10 ng/ml)'. NCIT:C20428 'Hepatocyte Growth Factor'.

Supp Data 1 legend (MOESM3): heavy = 'absence ... of HGF', and the ratio is described as 'HGF-treated (L) to untreated'. Supp Data 1: H of lane C = 'Nuc Ctl' (B in 'H/M ... B/A (Nuc Ctl/No int nuc)'); Methods: heavy cells 'warmed to 37 C in the absence of HGF'. 'untreated' is the value the sample-metadata template's treatment validator prescribes for controls (it is not an NCIT/EFO term, hence the validator warning).

Supp Data 1 names the M channel of lane C only 'No int nuclear' / 'No int nuc' (no internalisation); no source states whether this arm received HGF, and the Methods do not describe the medium arm at all.

claims.evidence: The surface-proteome protocol has no 37 C internalisation step: cells were biotinylated at 4 C, (heavy/light) MesNa-treated or not at 4 C, lysed.

Description of Supplementary Files (Supp Data 1 sheet 2 legend): 'Light-labelled cells (L) were treated with MesNa to remove biotin from the cell surface, whilst heavy-labelled cells were left untreated (H)'. Supp Data 1 sheet 'surface Red_NonRed', column 'Ratio L/H Normalized Expt1_D +red/-red (surface)': L = reduced (MesNa-stripped), H = non-reduced. Deposited proteinGroups.txt confirms the orientation in BOTH Expt1_D and Expt2_D: surface receptors have H/L >> 1 (TFRC 864 / 3.7, EGFR 21.7 / 18.5, EPHA2 28 / 150, ITGB1 27 / 12), i.e. biotin was stripped from the L channel. The main-text Methods/PRIDE prose ('Heavy-labelled cells were incubated with MesNa') contradicts this; the explicit supplementary legend and the data agree with each other and win. Expt2_D orientation is INFERRED from the ratio pattern (Supp Data 1 only reports Expt1_D). NCIT:C192 'Mesna'.

MOESM3 legend: 'heavy-labelled cells were left untreated (H)'. H channel of lanes D = '-red' (non-reduced) per Supp Data 1 and the deposited H/L ratios (see Mesna claim). 'untreated' per template guidance for controls.

mqpar.xml groups runs into Expt1_* (2017 acquisitions) and Expt2_* (2018 acquisitions); the paper (Fig. 1b legend) reports SILAC ratios 'from two independent experiments ((1) and (2))' and Supp Data 1 reports Expt1 and Expt2 columns side by side.
PRIDE organism Homo sapiens; H1299 is a human cell line (Cellosaurus OX NCBI_TaxID=9606).

Raw-file headers (2017 and 2018 batches) contain 'Q Exactive HF - Orbitrap MS' and 'Method of Q Exactive HF'; Methods: 'Orbitrap Q-Exactive HF'. PRIDE's instruments field ('Orbitrap Fusion Lumos') is wrong for this dataset (Lumos belongs to the companion TurboID dataset PXD027217).
Methods: 'The top ten most intense ions in the full MS were isolated for fragmentation' (top-10 DDA).

The column is the digestion enzyme (TERMS.tsv; sdrf-annotate technical-values.md 5.3). Methods: digested with trypsin (Trypsin gold, Promega). NOTE: the MaxQuant search used the Trypsin/P cleavage rule (mqpar <enzymes>Trypsin/P</enzymes>, MS:1001313), i.e. trypsin without the proline restriction; a reanalysis replicating the deposited search should use Trypsin/P.

They are triple-SILAC runs (all three channels quantified) whose channel->condition map is documented nowhere: paper, Supplementary Information, Description of Supplementary Files, Supplementary Data 1-3, Source Data, Peer Review File, PRIDE protocols and files/all, MaxQuant mqpar/parameters/summary/proteinGroups (experiment names only). Data Availability says 'available from the corresponding author on request', so no external repository exists. Unblocked by a channel map from the corresponding author (J.C. Norman). Recorded in annotations/BLOCKED.md.

Main-text Methods/PRIDE prose says heavy cells were MesNa-reduced in the surface experiment; the Description of Supplementary Files, Supplementary Data 1 and the deposited ratios all show the reverse (L = reduced, H = non-reduced), which is used. Expt2_D orientation is inferred from its ratio pattern; Supp Data 1 reports only Expt1_D.

Methods and PRIDE describe 2-state heavy/light SILAC, while the Results text, Supp Data 1 and the MaxQuant search are 3-state (L/M/H with M = Arg6/Lys4); the medium 'no internalisation' arm of lane C is described only by the Supp Data 1 header.
The lane-D medium channel (search slot exists, ~4% residual intensity, mqpar reQuantify=true) is treated as unused: no SDRF row.
Treatment of the no-internalisation (M) arm (HGF or not) is unknown -> not available; its 0 minute sampling time is inferred from the 'No int' label.

characteristics[treatment] encodes the per-sub-experiment contrast: HGF vs untreated (no HGF) in the nuclear lanes, Mesna vs untreated (not reduced) in the surface lanes. All nuclear-capture arms were also MesNa surface-reduced and warmed to 37 C; 'untreated' there means 'no HGF', following the authors' own wording.
Paper states 6 gel slices per lane; Expt1 lanes have 8 raw files (fractions 1-8). Annotated per the deposited files.
Validator warning: 'untreated' (template-prescribed control value) is not an NCIT/EFO term.
